items.text: Understand what a file editor is and why it is used in Linux
Know the difference between nano and vi/vim
Explain vi/vim's three modes: Command, Insert, and Last Line
Know what vi and vim stand for
Understand that vi is POSIX standard and available on every Linux system
Understand what wc does and what its three-number output means
Explain what grep does and why case sensitivity matters
Understand that sort does not modify the original file by default
Explain what the pipe operator | does and why it is powerful
Open, edit, save, and exit a file using nano (Ctrl+X → Y → Enter)
Open a file with vi and switch between all three modes
Type text in vi Insert Mode and save with :wq
Force-quit vi without saving using :q!
Use wc -l, wc -w, and wc -c to count file properties
Search for text in files using grep, grep -i, grep -n, and grep -r
Sort a file alphabetically, numerically, in reverse, and remove duplicates
Chain two or more commands together using the pipe operator
Navigate a vi file with h, j, k, l, gg, G, and :n
State what vi stands for (Visual Editor) and what vim stands for (Vi IMproved)
List the three vi/vim modes and how to enter and exit each one
Recall the correct :wq command to save and quit vi
State the wc output order: lines, words, characters
Know which grep flag ignores case (-i), shows line numbers (-n), and searches recursively (-r)
Explain that sort -u removes duplicate lines and sort does not modify the original file
Describe the pipe operator as feeding one command's output as another command's input
